common_name: Hawaii Blue Ageratum (Compact Dwarf Bedding Ageratum)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; seed needs light to germinate, so press into the surface rather than covering.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, pressing the fine seed into the surface without covering since it needs light to germinate. Hawaii is a classic ultra-dwarf ageratum series bred for a tight, uniform mounded habit that stays low and neat without pinching, unlike taller cut-flower ageratum types. It produces dense clusters of fuzzy, powder-puff sky-blue flowers held just above the foliage, ideal for edging and container fronts. Shearing lightly in midsummer refreshes bloom for fall.

common_name: Red Flash Ageratum (Unusual Brick-Red Floss Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; performs in full sun to light afternoon shade.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. Red Flash breaks from the usual blue-and-white ageratum palette with fuzzy flower clusters in a deep brick-red to rusty terracotta shade, set off by dark bronze-tinged green foliage. Its mounding, well-branched habit suits mixed containers and warm-toned borders where typical powder-blue ageratum would clash. It blooms steadily from early summer to frost and is more self-cleaning than older ageratum strains.

common_name: Helen Campbell Cleome (Classic White Heirloom Spider Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost; the tall stature and mildly thorny stems are best sited toward the back of a border, away from foot traffic.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost; Helen Campbell is an early-20th-century heirloom selection prized for pure white, spidery flower clusters with long, whisker-like stamens that open progressively up tall flower spikes through summer. Unlike newer compact, spineless cleome cultivars, it retains the traditional tall stature and mildly thorny stems of old-fashioned spider flower, making it best sited toward the back of a border or away from foot traffic. Flowers release a musky fragrance most noticeable at dusk, drawing hawkmoths and hummingbirds, and the plant self-sows readily once established.

common_name: Fragrant Cloud Nicotiana (Evening-Fragrant White Flowering Tobacco)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; site near a patio or window where evening scent can be enjoyed after sundown.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. Fragrant Cloud produces large, star-throated white tubular flowers on tall, upright stems, bred specifically for strong evening fragrance that intensifies at dusk, unlike many modern day-blooming bedding nicotianas selected mainly for daytime color. Its taller habit suits the middle to back of a border or a container placed near a patio or open window where the scent can be enjoyed after sundown. Plants bloom continuously from early summer through frost without deadheading.
